chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Sahl ibn al-Yasaʿ al-Ashʿarī, from his father, from Abī al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him: May a man perform salat (prayer) while in his dye, if he is in a state of taharah (ritual purity)? He said: Yes.

key_terms.الرَّجُلُ: the man; the legal subject being asked about
key_terms.خِضَابِهِ: his dye; the state or substance of coloration being discussed
key_terms.طُهْرٍ: ritual purity; a state of taharah required for salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) while wearing dye if one is in a state of taharah (ritual purity)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that performing salat (prayer) while one has dye on oneself is permissible, provided the person is in a state of taharah (ritual purity). Its significance is that the presence of dye itself does not invalidate salat (prayer) when ritual purity is maintained.
